title: Existence of K-flat resolutions on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. For every cochain complex $\mathcal G^\bullet$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] there exist a K-flat complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] whose terms are flat $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] which is surjective in every degree.

proof.text: Choose a tower $E_n,t_n,q_n$ from [lem-pc-flat-truncation-tower]. Each $E_n$ is bounded above with flat terms, and $q_n:E_n\to\tau_{\le n}G$ is a degreewise epimorphic quasi-isomorphism. The compositions $q_n\iota_n$ commute strictly with $t_n$.

Let $B=\bigoplus_nE_n$, $\phi=1-\operatorname{shift}_t$, and $s=\sum_nq_n\iota_n:B\to G$. Coproduct extensionality and the strict compatibility give $\phi s=0$. The mapping-cone desc construction, with zero shifted component and unshifted component $s$, therefore gives $f:\operatorname{Cone}(\phi)\to G$. By [lem-pc-kflat-closure], each bounded-above flat $E_n$ is K-flat and its telescope is K-flat. Evaluation preserves coproducts, so each $B^i$ is flat by the coproduct clause of that same lemma. Each cone term is isomorphic to $B^{i+1}\oplus B^i$, hence flat by the same clause for a two-element indexing set. Transport flatness across the tensor-right isomorphism. Reindex the small indexing types by ULift into the site universe when applying the countable coproduct clause.

Apply [lem-pc-flat-truncation-telescope-comparison] to $f$, whose restrictions to the shifted and unshifted summands are those of the cone desc construction. This makes $f$ a quasi-isomorphism. In a fixed degree $i$, choose $n=i_{\ge0}+1$ so that $i<n$. The component of the truncation inclusion $\iota_n$ in degree $i$ is an isomorphism. Hence $q_n^i\iota_n^i$ is epi. It factors through $f^i$ by the coproduct inclusion followed by the unshifted cone inclusion, so $f^i$ is epi. These give all four asserted properties of the explicitly constructed telescope.
